approachQuestion.prompt: A row of integer levels evolves in simultaneous rounds. In each round remove every entry whose immediate left neighbor at the START of that round has a strictly greater level; the first entry is never removed that round. Continue until a round removes nothing. Return the number of rounds that removed at least one entry. Example: [5,1,2,3] returns 3, with rows [5,2,3], [5,3], then [5]. Equal neighbors do not trigger removal. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Scan left to right, storing (level, removalRound). Start delay=0. Pop while the top level is at most the current level, setting delay=max(delay,popped removalRound). If the stack becomes empty set delay=0; otherwise increase delay by 1. Push the current pair and maximize the answer over delays.
options.feedback: Smaller or equal predecessors cannot directly remove the current entry, but may delay exposure to a surviving greater predecessor. The maximum removed-block delay determines when that exposure occurs; if no greater predecessor remains, the current entry survives.

options.text: Return 1 if the original row has any decreasing adjacent pair, otherwise return 0.
options.feedback: New decreasing adjacencies appear later. For [5,1,2,3], the process lasts 3 rounds, not 1.

options.text: Use the delay stack, but add every popped removalRound instead of taking their maximum before adding 1.
options.feedback: Several predecessors disappear in parallel. For [10,3,2,4,5], the correct rounds for the last two entries are 2 and 3; summing popped delays makes the final delay 4 instead of 3.

options.text: Repeatedly scan the entire current row, mark all entries with greater left neighbors, and build the next row after the scan.
options.feedback: This simulates correctly, but [n,1,2,...,n-1] removes just one entry per round and repeatedly scans long rows, causing quadratic work.

feedback.reason: Track removal delays across dominated blockers instead of simulating every round.
details: Assign each entry its disappearance round, or zero if it survives. Remove smaller or equal stack candidates while retaining the largest delay among them. A remaining larger predecessor removes the entry one round after that delay; without one the entry survives. Track the maximum assigned round.

Simultaneous deletion means a blocker may disappear only after earlier blockers have disappeared. Carry the largest popped delay, then add one if a larger predecessor remains. Immediate sequential deletion would model different rounds.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For stack-removal-delays, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the original row length. Use an iterative stack of level/round pairs and a scalar maximum. No round-by-round row copies are made.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One delay update per pop bounds the full simulation to linear work.
details: Each entry is pushed once and popped at most once. Maximum-delay updates cost constant time per pop, giving O(n) total time. A strictly decreasing row retains n stack entries, so auxiliary space is O(n).
